title: Authentic Nepali Mustang Aloo
description: Mustang Aloo is a traditional Nepali potato dish from the high-altitude Mustang region, famous for its bold Himalayan flavors. Made with locally grown potatoes, mustard oil, timur, garlic, and aromatic spices, this dish delivers a perfect balance of crispy texture, spicy heat, and earthy mountain flavors.

ingredients.title: For the Potatoes
items: Mustang potatoes (or baby potatoes) – 800 g, washed and cleaned

ingredients.title: For the Spiced Mustard Oil Base
items: Dried red chilies – 3–4, broken into pieces
Timur (Nepali Sichuan pepper) – 1½ tsp, lightly crushed

ingredients.title: For Finishing
items: Fresh coriander leaves – small handful, chopped

instruction.title: Step 1 – Preparing the Potatoes
steps: Wash Mustang potatoes thoroughly to remove soil.
Boil potatoes in salted water until just tender but still firm.
Drain, cool slightly, and cut into large bite-sized pieces. Keep the skin on for authentic rustic flavor.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Creating the Mustard Oil Flavor
steps: Heat mustard oil in a heavy pan until it reaches smoking point, then reduce the heat.
Add garlic, ginger, and dried red chilies. Fry until aromatic and lightly golden.
Add crushed timur and allow it to release its citrusy Himalayan aroma.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Spicing the Potatoes
steps: Add turmeric, cumin powder, coriander powder, chili powder, black pepper, and salt.
Stir the spices quickly in the oil to bloom their flavors without burning.
Add boiled potatoes and gently toss until every piece is coated with the spice mixture.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Crisping the Mustang Aloo
steps: Cook on medium heat for 8–12 minutes, turning occasionally.
Allow the potatoes to develop a golden crispy exterior while absorbing the Himalayan spices.
Avoid stirring too aggressively to keep the potato pieces intact.

instruction.title: Step 5 – Final Touch
steps: Turn off the heat and add lemon juice.
Garnish with fresh coriander, spring onions, and roasted sesame seeds.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving to allow flavors to settle.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve hot with traditional Nepali dal bhat.
Enjoy as a snack with chiura (beaten rice) and achar.
Pairs beautifully with sekuwa, grilled meat, or Himalayan tea.
Serve as a rustic side dish for a Nepali mountain-style meal.

chefTips: Use firm potatoes like Mustang potatoes because they hold their shape and become crispy outside.
Mustard oil should be heated properly before cooking to remove its raw pungency.
Timur is the signature spice that gives authentic Nepali mountain flavor.
Keep potato pieces slightly large to achieve a rustic traditional texture.
For deeper flavor, rest the cooked Mustang Aloo for 10–15 minutes before serving.
